meta.guideline: STRESS - Strengthening The Reporting of Empirical Simulation Studies
meta.citation: Monks, T., Currie, C. S. M., Onggo, B. S., Robinson, S., Kunc, M., & Taylor, S. J. E. (2019). Strengthening the reporting of empirical simulation studies: Introducing the STRESS guidelines. Journal of Simulation, 13(1), 55-67.
meta.licence: Checklist text (c) 2018 Monks, Currie, Onggo, Robinson, Kunc & Taylor, from the Supplementary material of doi:10.1080/17477778.2018.1442155, published Open Access under CC BY 4.0. Reproduced verbatim; the supplements' typographical slips are preserved deliberately so that the authoritative wording is not altered.
meta.numbering_note: Numbering follows the published Supplementary checklists (3.2 Pre-processing, 3.3 Input parameters). The article's Table 3 (PDF p. 7 / journal p. 60) prints these two items in the opposite order (3.2 Input parameters, 3.3 Pre-processing).
meta.identical_items_note: Items 4.2 and 6.1 are word-for-word identical in all three variants; 1.1 is identical in SD and ABS; 2.4 in DES and ABS; 3.2 in DES and SD; 5.4 in DES and ABS. All other items differ in every variant.
meta.detection_note: detection_keywords are the skill's own aid for inferring the paradigm, drawn from the vocabulary of each checklist. STRESS itself gives no detection rule; an inferred paradigm must be confirmed with the user (SOFT pause) or stated as inferred in the report header.

hybrid_interface_check.title: Interface between simulation methods (hybrid models only)
hybrid_interface_check.basis: Monks et al. (2019) section 6, Q 'I have developed a hybrid simulation model', PDF p. 9 / journal p. 62. Not a numbered STRESS item; the paper's provisional advice (section 8, PDF p. 12 / journal p. 65, defers hybrid and distributed simulation to later work).
hybrid_interface_check.recommendation_verbatim: it is recommended to apply both the STRESS-DES and STRESS-SD guidelines to strengthen the reporting of the appropriate model components. However, some adaptation of the guidelines is needed to handle the interface between the DES and SD components of the models. It is recommended that authors report how the two (or more) methods communicate.
hybrid_interface_check.check: Does the document report how the two (or more) simulation methods communicate (what information passes between components, when, and in which direction)?

items.title: Purpose of the model
items.recommendation: Explain the background and objectives for the model.
items.pdf_locator: Table 3 P7/J60; rationale section 5.2 P6/J59

items.title: Model Outputs
items.recommendation: Define all quantitative performance measures that are reported, using equations where necessary. Specify how and when they are calculated during the model run along with how any measures of error such as confidence intervals are calculated.
items.pdf_locator: Table 3 P7/J60; section 5.2 P6/J59

items.title: Experimentation Aims
items.recommendation: If the model has been used for experimentation, state the objectives that it was used to investigate.
items.applicability: Conditional: applies only if the model has been used for experimentation beyond the base run (R21). Sub-points are audited only for the type(s) of experimentation actually used (R22; skill interpretation - only sub-point c carries an explicit '(if appropriate)').

subitems.title: Scenario based analysis
subitems.recommendation: Scenario based analysis – Provide a name and description for each scenario, providing a rationale for the choice of scenarios and ensure that item 2.3 (below) is completed.

subitems.title: Design of experiments
subitems.recommendation: Design of experiments – Provide details of the overall design of the experiments with reference to performance measures and their parameters (provide further details in data below).
subitems.applicability: When a designed experiment is used.

subitems.title: Simulation Optimisation
subitems.recommendation: Simulation Optimisation – (if appropriate) Provide full details of what is to be optimised, the parameters that were included and the algorithm(s) that was be used. Where possible provide a citation of the algorithm(s).
subitems.applicability: '(if appropriate)' - when simulation optimisation is used.

items.pdf_locator: Table 3 P7/J60; section 5.2 P6/J59

items.title: Base model overview diagram
items.recommendation: Describe the base model using appropriate diagrams and description. This could include one or more process flow, activity cycle or equivalent diagrams sufficient to describe the model to readers. Avoid complicated diagrams in the main text. The goal is to describe the breadth and depth of the model with respect to the system being studied.
items.pdf_locator: Table 3 P7/J60; section 5.3 P6-7/J59-60; Table 2 principle 6 P7/J60

items.title: Base model logic
items.recommendation: Give details of the base model logic. Give additional model logic details sufficient to communicate to the reader how the model works.
items.pdf_locator: Table 3 P7/J60; section 5.3 P6/J59

items.title: Scenario logic
items.recommendation: Give details of the logical difference between the base case model and scenarios (if any). This could be incorporated as text or where differences are substantial could be incorporated in the same manner as 2.2.
items.applicability: Conditional: '(if any)' - Not applicable when the study has no scenarios (R23). If scenarios exist and the document states the logic is unchanged, that statement is the evidence.
items.pdf_locator: Table 3 P7/J60; section 5.3 P6/J59

items.title: Algorithms
items.recommendation: Provide further detail on any algorithms in the model that (for example) mimic complex or manual processes in the real world (i.e. scheduling of arrivals/appointments/operations/maintenance, operation of a conveyor system, machine breakdowns, etc.). Sufficient detail should be included (or referred to in other published work) for the algorithms to be reproducible. Pseudo-code may be used to describe an algorithm.
items.applicability: Conditional: 'any algorithms' - Not applicable when no such algorithm is evident anywhere in the model description (R24). A reference to other published work satisfies the detail requirement.
items.pdf_locator: Table 3 P7/J60

items.title: Components
items.applicability: Audit each sub-item separately; the sub-items are the paradigm-specific building blocks of the model.

subitems.title: Entities
subitems.recommendation: Give details of all entities within the simulation including a description of their role in the model and a description of all their attributes.

subitems.title: Activities
subitems.recommendation: Describe the activities that entities engage in within the model. Provide details of entity routing into and out of the activity.

subitems.title: Resources
subitems.recommendation: List all the resources included within the model and which activities make use of them.

subitems.title: Queues
subitems.recommendation: Give details of the assumed queuing discipline used in the model (e.g. First in First Out, Last in First Out, prioritisation, etc.). Where one or more queues have a different discipline from the rest, provide a list of queues, indicating the queuing discipline used for each. If reneging, balking or jockeying occur, etc., provide details of the rules. Detail any delays or capacity constraints on the queues.
subitems.applicability: Reneging/balking/jockeying rules only if those behaviours occur.

subitems.title: Entry/Exit Points
subitems.recommendation: Give details of the model boundaries i.e. all arrival and exit points of entities. Detail the arrival mechanism (e.g. ‘thinning’ to mimic a non-homogenous Poisson process or balking)

items.pdf_locator: Table 4 P8/J61 (minor wording differences: 'baulking' vs 'balking'); section 5.3 P7/J60

items.title: Data sources
items.recommendation:
List and detail all data sources. Sources may include:
- Interviews with stakeholders,
- Samples of routinely collected data,
- Prospectively collected samples for the purpose of the simulation study,
- Public domain data published in either academic or organisational literature. Provide, where possible, the link and DOI to the data or reference to published literature.
All data source descriptions should include details of the sample size, sample date ranges and use within the study.
items.applicability: Link/DOI 'where possible' (R33): its absence alone does not make the item Missing when the source is described or referenced.
items.pdf_locator: Table 3 P7/J60; section 5.4 P7/J60; Table 5 P9/J62

items.title: Pre-processing
items.recommendation: Provide details of any data manipulation that has taken place before its use in the simulation, e.g. interpolation to account for missing data or the removal of outliers.
items.applicability: 'any data manipulation': silence is Missing; an explicit statement that no pre-processing was performed is Addressed (R26).
items.pdf_locator: Table 3 P7/J60 prints this as item 3.3 (numbering differs); section 5.4 P7/J60

items.title: Input parameters
items.recommendation:
List all input variables in the model. Provide a description of their use and include parameter values. For stochastic inputs provide details of any continuous, discrete or empirical distributions used along with all associated parameters. Give details of all time dependent parameters and correlation.
Clearly state:
- Base case data
- Data use in experimentation, where different from the base case.
- Where optimisation or design of experiments has been used, state the range of values that parameters can take.
Where theoretical distributions are used, state how these were selected and prioritised above other candidate distributions.
items.applicability: Unconditional: the list of inputs with values and the base case data. Conditional clauses (R27): stochastic inputs -> distributions and parameters; experimentation -> data where different; optimisation/DoE -> parameter ranges; theoretical distributions -> selection rationale.
items.pdf_locator: Table 3 P7/J60 prints this as item 3.2 (numbering differs); section 5.4 P7/J60; Table 5 P9/J62

items.title: Assumptions
items.recommendation: Where data or knowledge of the real system is unavailable what assumptions are included in the model? This might include parameter values, distributions or routing logic within the model.
items.pdf_locator: Table 3 P7/J60; section 5.4 P7/J60

items.title: Initialisation
items.recommendation:
Report if the system modelled is terminating or non-terminating. State if a warm-up period has been used, its length and the analysis method used to select it. For terminating systems state the stopping condition.
State what if any initial model conditions have been included, e.g., pre-loaded queues and activities. Report whether initialisation of these variables is deterministic or stochastic.
items.applicability: Unconditional: terminating/non-terminating statement; a statement on warm-up (even 'none'); statement on initial conditions (even 'none'). Conditional (R28): warm-up length and selection method if a warm-up is used; stopping condition for terminating systems; deterministic/stochastic initialisation if initial conditions exist.
items.pdf_locator: Table 3 P7/J60; section 5.5 P7/J60; Table 6 P9/J62

items.title: Run length
items.recommendation: Detail the run length of the simulation model and time units.
items.pdf_locator: Table 3 P7/J60; section 5.5 P7/J60; Table 6 P9/J62

items.title: Estimation approach
items.recommendation: State the method used to account for the stochasticity: For example, two common methods are multiple replications or batch means. Where multiple replications have been used, state the number of replications and for batch means, indicate the batch length and whether the batch means procedure is standard, spaced or overlapping. For both procedures provide a justification for the methods used and the number of replications/size of batches.
items.applicability: Assumes a stochastic model (R29). A deterministic DES is unusual: mark Not applicable via R16 and flag it. Requires method, count (replications or batch details) AND a justification; count without justification is Partially addressed.
items.pdf_locator: Table 3 P7/J60; section 5.5 P7/J60; Table 6 P9/J62

items.title: Software or programming language
items.recommendation:
State the operating system and version and build number.
State the name, version and build number of commercial or open source DES software that the model is implemented in.
State the name and version of general-purpose programming languages used (e.g. Python 3.5).
Where frameworks and libraries have been used provide all details including version numbers.
items.applicability: Operating system and simulation software/language with versions are unconditional; frameworks/libraries clause applies when any are used.
items.pdf_locator: Table 3 P7/J60; section 5.6 P7-9/J60-62; Table 7 P10/J63

items.title: Random sampling
items.recommendation:
State the algorithm used to generate random samples in the software/programming language used e.g. Mersenne Twister.
If common random numbers are used, state how seeds (or random number streams) are distributed among sampling processes.
items.applicability: Not applicable for deterministic models (R16, PDF section 5.6: 'Relevant only for stochastic models'). Second sentence conditional on common random numbers being used (R30).
items.pdf_locator: Table 3 P7/J60; section 5.6 P9/J62; Table 7 P10/J63

items.title: Model execution
items.recommendation:
State the event processing mechanism used e.g. three phase, event, activity, process interaction.
Note that in some commercial software the event processing mechanism may not be published. In these cases authors should adhere to item 5.1 software recommendations.
State all priority rules included if entities/activities compete for resources.
If the model is parallel, distributed and/or use grid or cloud computing, etc., state and preferably reference the technology used. For parallel and distributed simulations the time management algorithms used. If the HLA is used then state the version of the standard, which run-time infrastructure (and version), and any supporting documents (FOMs, etc.)
items.applicability: Event processing mechanism unconditional, but an unpublished commercial mechanism plus complete 5.1 detail counts as Addressed (R18, R31). Priority rules only if entities/activities compete for resources; parallel/distributed/HLA clauses only if such technology is used (R31).
items.pdf_locator: Table 3 P7/J60; section 5.6 P9/J62; Table 7 P10/J63

items.title: System Specification
items.recommendation: State the model run time and specification of hardware used. This is particularly important for large scale models that require substantial computing power. For parallel, distributed and/or use grid or cloud computing, etc. state the details of all systems used in the implementation (processors, network, etc.)
items.applicability: Never automatically Not applicable; for small models a Missing is noted as low impact (R17). Parallel/distributed clause conditional (R32).

subitems.title: Environment
subitems.recommendation: Describe the environment agents interact within, indicating its structure, and how it is generated. For example, are agents bound within a homogeneous grid, or do they have continuous movement through a detailed landscape incorporating geographic or environmental information?

subitems.title: Agents
subitems.recommendation:
List all agents and agent groups within the simulation. Include a description of their role in the model, their possible states, state transitions, and all their attributes.
Describe all decision-making rules that agents follow in either algorithmic or equation form. Where relevant authors should report:
- The data that agents access (I.e. internal attributes or external information from the environment) and how it is used.
- The objectives agents seek to achieve.
- The algorithms, optimisations, heuristics and rules that agents use to achieve objectives.
- How agents work together within a group along with any rules for changes in group membership.
- Predictions of future events and adaptive action.
subitems.applicability: Bulleted points 'Where relevant' - audit those that apply to the model's agents.

subitems.title: Interaction Topology
subitems.recommendation:
Describe how agents and agent groupings are connected with each other in the model define:
- with whom agents can interact,
- how recipients of interactions are selected
- what frequency interaction occurs.
- How agents handle and assign priorities to concurrent events
It is recommended that interactions are described using a combination of equations pseudo-code and logic diagrams.
Report how interactions are affected by agent states and the environment state

subitems.title: Entry / Exit
subitems.recommendation: Where relevant, define how agents are created and destroyed in the model.
subitems.applicability: 'Where relevant' - Not applicable when the agent population is fixed and the document says so (R25).

items.title: Data sources
items.recommendation:
List and detail all data sources. Sources may include:
- Interviews with stakeholders
- samples of routinely collected data,
- prospectively collected samples for the purpose of the simulation study,
- public domain data published in either academic or organisational literature. Provide, where possible, the link and DOI to the data or reference to published literature.
All data source descriptions should include details of the sample size, date ranges and use within the study.
items.applicability: Link/DOI 'where possible' (R33).
items.pdf_locator: Table 3 P7/J60; section 5.4 P7/J60; Table 5 P9/J62

items.title: Pre-processing
items.recommendation: Provide details of any data manipulation or filtering that has taken place before its use in the simulation, e.g. interpolation to account for missing data, removal of outliers or filtering of large scale data.
items.applicability: 'any data manipulation or filtering': silence is Missing; an explicit statement that no pre-processing was performed is Addressed (R26).
items.pdf_locator: Table 3 P7/J60 prints this as item 3.3 (numbering differs); section 5.4 P7/J60

items.title: Input parameters
items.recommendation:
List all input parameters in the model, providing a description of each parameter and the values used. For stochastic inputs provide details of any continuous, discrete or empirical distributions used along with all associated parameters. Where applicable define the time/spatial dependence of parameters and any correlation structure.
Clearly state:
- Base case inputs
- Inputs used in experimentation, where different from the base case.
- Where optimisation or design of experiments has been used, state the range of values that parameters can take.
Where theoretical distributions are used, state how, , these were selected and prioritised above other candidate distributions.
items.applicability: Unconditional: the list of inputs with values and the base case inputs. Conditional clauses (R27): stochastic inputs; time/spatial dependence 'Where applicable'; experimentation inputs; optimisation/DoE ranges; theoretical distribution selection.
items.pdf_locator: Table 3 P7/J60 prints this as item 3.2 (numbering differs); section 5.4 P7/J60

items.title: Assumptions
items.recommendation: Where data or knowledge of the real system is unavailable, state and justify the assumptions used to set input parameter values and distributions; agent interactions or behaviour; or model logic.
items.applicability: Requires both a statement AND a justification of assumptions; a list without justification is Partially addressed.

items.title: Initialisation
items.recommendation:
State if a warm-up period has been used, its length and the analysis method used to select it.
State what if any initial agent and environmental conditions have been included. For example, the initial agent population size, agent states and attributes, initial agent network structure(s), and resources within the environment. Report whether initialisation of these variables is deterministic or stochastic.
items.applicability: Unconditional: a statement on warm-up (even 'none'; the supplement asks unconditionally, unlike PDF section 5.5's 'where appropriate for stochastic ABS' - discrepancy D10); statement on initial agent/environment conditions. Conditional (R28): warm-up length and selection method if used; deterministic/stochastic initialisation if initial conditions exist.

items.title: Run length
items.recommendation: Detail the run length of the simulation model and time units.

items.title: Estimation approach
items.recommendation: State if the model is deterministic or stochastic. If the model is stochastic, state the number of replications that have been used. If an alternative estimation method has been used (e.g. batch means), provide full details.
items.applicability: The deterministic/stochastic statement is unconditional - an explicit 'deterministic' statement is Addressed (R29). Replications (or alternative method details) required only if stochastic.

items.title: Software or programming language
items.recommendation:
State the operating system and version and build number.
State the name, version and build number of commercial or open source ABS software that the model is implemented in.
State the name and version of general-purpose programming languages used (e.g. Python 3.5.2). Where packages, frameworks and libraries have been used provide all detailed including version numbers.
items.applicability: Operating system and software/language with versions unconditional; packages clause only if any are used.

items.title: Random sampling
items.recommendation: State the algorithm or package used to generate random samples within the software/programming language used e.g. Mersenne Twister or Java.Random version x.y
items.applicability: Not applicable for deterministic models (R16; PDF section 5.6; ABS-supp 4.3 asks for the deterministic/stochastic statement).

items.title: Model execution
items.recommendation:
If the ABS model has a time component, describe how time is modelled (e.g. fixed time steps or discrete-event). State the order of variable updating within the model. In time-stepped execution state how concurrent events are resolved.
If the model is parallel, distributed and/or use grid or cloud computing, etc., state and preferably reference the technology used. For parallel and distributed simulations the time management algorithms used. If the HLA is used then state the version of the standard, which run-time infrastructure (and version), and any supporting documents (FOMs, etc.)
items.applicability: Time-modelling clause 'If the ABS model has a time component' (almost always); concurrency clause only for time-stepped execution; parallel/distributed/HLA clauses only if such technology is used (R31). Unpublished commercial mechanism plus full 5.1 detail counts as Addressed (R18).

items.title: System Specification
items.recommendation: State the model run time and specification of hardware used. This is particularly important for large scale models that require substantial computing power. For parallel, distributed and/or use grid or cloud computing, etc. state the details of all systems used in the implementation (processors, network, etc.)
items.applicability: Never automatically Not applicable; for small models a Missing is noted as low impact (R17). Parallel/distributed clause conditional (R32).

items.title: Computer Model Sharing Statement
items.recommendation: Describe how someone could obtain the model described in the paper, the simulation software and any other associated software (or hardware) needed to reproduce the results. Provide, where possible, the link and DOIs to these.
items.applicability: 'Models are available on request', a secure/local directory, or a repository link all satisfy the statement (PDF section 5.7). Link/DOI 'where possible' (R33). A code link does not satisfy items 2.x-5.x (R7).
